title: Finite affine ind-etale Cech exactness for comparison pullbacks of injectives
statement: Let Y be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme], J an injective abelian sheaf on Y_et [def-sp-injective-resolutions, def-weil-pbc-etale-site], and F = nu_Y^{-1}J for the comparison inverse image [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Let V be an affine ind-etale Y-object [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-basis]. For a finite pro-etale covering U_i -> V whose nonempty repeated intersections are affine ind-etale Y-objects, the ordered Cech complex of F [def-weil-pbc-site-cech-complex] is exact at every degree q+1, for q a natural number. Intersections include the one-factor terms, so the members themselves belong to the basis up to isomorphism. The empty covering is allowed.

source.place: Tag 099U, lemma-affine-vanishing, verification of condition (3); https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/099U

proof.text: For an arbitrary positive-degree cocycle c, apply the finite affine comparison cocycle-descent theorem. It gives a finite etale covering T_i -> W on the original Y_et site, a cocycle c_prime of its categorical Cech complex with coefficients J, and a morphism of complexes phi carrying c_prime to c. This step does not use injectivity.

Apply injective_sheaf_cech_acyclic to J on Y_et and this actual covering. Convert its vanishing homology in degree q+1 to ExactAt and then use ShortComplex.ab_exact_iff to obtain a primitive b of c_prime. This uses injectivity only on the original Y_et, never on V_et or on the pro-etale site.

Take phi.f q b as a primitive of c. The chain-map equation phi.comm q (q+1), evaluated at b, identifies its differential with phi.f (q+1) applied to the differential of b. Substitute the primitive identity and the cocycle-lift identity. The component formula exactAt_cechComplex_iff concludes exactness. This argument includes the empty family through the descent theorem.
